title: Session-anchored log swarm consolidator for ordered, deduplicated structured ingest
creator: Marco Hernandez
description: Problem: Flaky service-to-service bursts produce highly out-of-order, duplicate structured log fragments that cause high cardinality and noisy dashboards in Loki/ELK, and increase tail latency due to cold KV-cache misses. Goal: build an edge-stage consolidator that groups bursty log "swarm" payloads by session/correlation hints, performs probabilistic deduplication, enforces ordering guarantees per session window, and emits compacted, watermark-marked batches to the upstream ingest pipeline. The component must be tenant-safe, memory-bounded, and able to degrade gracefully (sample-preserve fallback) when under sustained load. Non-goals: replacing long-term storage, implementing full schema evolution engine (this will emit a normalized JSON envelope pointing to schema versions).
acceptance_criteria: Consolidator accepts structured log events with correlation hint fields and emits ordered batches to the existing ingress topic (Kafka) compatible with current Loki/ELK adapters.
End-to-end latency for normal bursts is <= 200ms median and <= 1s 99th after consolidation (measured at the consolidator output).
Deduplication reduces redundant event count by >= 60% for synthetic burst tests with jitter/duplicates.
Component exposes metrics: sessions_open, batches_emitted, dedup_rate, memory_pressure, backpressure_trips, watermark_lag.
Rollout can be toggled per-tenant via runtime flag; default off for high-risk tenants.
Automated integration tests and a canary job with production-like traffic exist in CI and pass consistently.
implementation_notes: Design: local in-memory session windows keyed by tenant+session_hint; use compacted LRU with time-based eviction and probabilistic bloom filters to detect duplicates across bursts.

Backpressure: if memory threshold reached, emit best-effort sampled output with a header 'x-consolidator-sampled: true' and increment backpressure metric; route full payloads to cold-path storage for re-ingestion.
Ordering: guarantee per-session monotonic sequence when sequence numbers present; otherwise use event_time plus ingest_arrival to produce a stable ordering within watermark window.
Compatibility: output envelope includes original correlation ids, dedup checksum, schema_version, and watermark timestamp to allow downstream reassembly and ordered indexing in Loki/ELK.
Resource constraints: tune default window to 250ms/1s depending on tenant burstiness profiles and provide per-tenant overrides via Console.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (internal): deploy to observability-staging with synthetic burst harness; validate metrics and dedup rates against benchmarks.
Phase 2 (canary): enable for 5 low-risk tenants with conservative windows and monitor dashboards for dropped logs and dashboard regressions for 48h.
Phase 3 (gradual): ramp to 25% traffic across tenants with dynamic sampling thresholds and automatic fallback enabled.
Phase 4 (ga): enable by default with per-tenant opt-out; publish runbook and update Console gating UI.
monitoring: Create Grafana panel: consolidator overview (sessions_open, dedup_rate, memory_pressure), alert when memory_pressure > 75% for >5m.
Alert: dedup_rate drops below 5% for 30m (indicates mis-configuration) -> P1 paging to Oncall Observability.
Dashboards: add latency distribution by tenant and 99th watermark_lag; add Loki ingestion success ratio after consolidator.
SLO: ensure consolidator availability >= 99.9% during canary and GA phases.
